rationale: Supply a missing numbered gloss for the existing Detransitive Part. Pass. travel predicate, supported by three independent new contexts.

data.turoyo: Səmme məštuṯo l aḥuno du paša. Raxu aḥuno du paša, naḥiti af faroše aʕme, kəmsayri.
data.translation: Sie bereiteten dem Bruder des Fürsten das Hochzeitsfest. Er sass auf und ritt mit den Rittern aus zum Turnier.

rationale: First active intransitive II.2 example; explicit mounting/riding context and no caused-traveller object.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (97/46)

data.turoyo: <...> Aməlle l babux, d obelan xarǧiye, howina msayyər, əzzano bu papur ʕal u baḥar, kərxina bi arʕo w mətkayfina, əxlina, šotina. <...>
data.translation: <...> Bruder, sage deinem Vater, er solle uns Reisegeld geben, daß wir auf Reisen gehen. Wir wollen mit dem Dampfer auf dem Meere fahren und in der Welt herumstreifen, uns vergnügen, essen und trinken. <...>

rationale: Thin Detransitive Part. Pass. cell; explicit travelling by steamer and first-person plural howina.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (97/136)

data.turoyo: Hano ste, bat tawfiqat d aloho an naʕimani, u aḥuno w Aḥmad kowən msayyər, kərxi barban du baḥar. Ḥərre: kaṯəlle ṣabaṭ ʕal u baḥarano.
data.translation: Durch Gottesfügung gingen sein Bruder und Aḥmad am Meerentlang spazieren. Da sahen sie eine Kiste auf dem Meere auf sich zu treiben.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Part. Pass. cell; named plural subjects with kowən and invariant msayyər.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (112/220)

data.turoyo: Məlle: “Ya ann aḥunonayḏi, adyawma lo kəzzano lu ṣaydo. Kfayšina adyawma bi walaye, howina msayyər, kərxina bi walayaṯe.”
data.translation: Er sprach: Brüder, heute gehen wir nicht auf die Jagd. Wir wollen heute in dieser Stadt bleiben und in ihr spazieren gehen. -

rationale: Thin Detransitive Part. Pass. cell; city walk opposed to hunting, clear limited outing.

summary: All six occurrences checked. Existing 88/19 time-passing and 97/130 walking quotations are not duplicated. Active kəmsayri has no travel-caused object; the limited new gloss does not infer a special tournament sense from the free German translation.

howina/hawən/kowən msayyər is repeatedly used of plural travellers without an external sender. Retain the glossary's Detransitive Part. Pass. label; describe its non-agentive outing state in notes rather than replacing the label.

The same-looking msayyər occurs with plural subjects; the input does not warrant changing it to a reconstructed plural form. Imitated Arabic morphology or a contact pathway cannot be established solely from the inherited etymology.
Active sense 1 already treats time passing and keeping someone waiting; no separate light-verb or time-object sense is added.
Is active kəmsayri in PrS 39/72 a regular intransitive use of II, or does this dialect neutralize an expected Detransitive distinction?
Is msayyər invariant in the plural howina/hawən/kowən construction, or a conventional predicate with a separate number history? Confirm against speech.
Does the single PrS context specifically mean a recreational ride, ceremonial riding or ordinary going about? The proposed gloss excludes an unsupported technical tournament meaning.
